# NPM tarball integrity manifest
#
# NOT generated by CI. Written by `scripts/install-npm.sh` when a maintainer
# runs it locally; no workflow invokes that script and no workflow appends
# here on tag push. The entries below therefore describe the last LOCAL
# build, not the published package, and this file is absent from the `files:`
# array in npm/package.json — it does not travel inside the tarball. See
# npm/INTEGRITY.md §SHA-256 tarball manifest (deferred control).
# PLAN-025 Batch I F-comp-002: file reset to exactly 1 line (the tarball of
# the local build at that time) — previously accumulated 51 stale entries
# across rebuilds, which confused adopter integrity checks.
#
# Regeneration — run the writer that actually produces these lines:
#
#   bash scripts/install-npm.sh
#
# It builds the tarball, hashes it with `sha256sum` (or `shasum -a 256`, or
# python hashlib as a last resort), and replaces the line for that filename
# in place. Manual equivalent, when you want the digest without re-staging:
#
#   cd npm && TARBALL=$(npm pack --json | python3 -c \
#     'import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)[0]["filename"])') && \
#     shasum -a 256 "$TARBALL"      # GNU: sha256sum "$TARBALL"
#
# The previously documented `npm pack --dry-run --json | jq -r '.[0].shasum'`
# CANNOT regenerate this file and is not a substitute: npm's `.shasum` is the
# legacy SHA-1 of the tarball, and it carries no filename, so it produces
# neither the algorithm nor the format of the lines below. `--dry-run` also
# writes no tarball to hash.
#
# Each line below maps: <sha256>  <tarball-name>
# Appended ONLY by a local `scripts/install-npm.sh` run.
#
79c6d7772ad40e92aac1c6349f891af254f7e399aebe63276bfafb8362e769aa  ceo-orchestration-1.0.0.tgz
